claim: Organizations should begin PQC migration by inventorying cryptographic assets.
Crypto agility helps systems swap cryptographic algorithms more easily.
NIST standardized ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA for post-quantum cryptography.
description: Supported factual claim about NIST standards

claim: Hybrid key exchange combines classical and post-quantum algorithms.
description: Supported definition of hybrid key exchange

claim: Current quantum computers can break RSA-2048 today.
description: High-risk unsupported claim - quantum cannot break RSA-2048 yet

claim: All organizations must immediately remove every classical algorithm.
description: Extreme recommendation not supported by sources

claim: PQC migration has no interoperability risks.
description: False claim - interoperability is a known challenge

claim: Quantum computers will break all cryptography within 5 years.
AES-256 is believed to be quantum-resistant.
PQC algorithms have larger key sizes than classical algorithms.
Organizations should test PQC in non-production environments first.
Harvest now, decrypt later attacks are a theoretical concern only.
description: Partially supported - concern is real but impact is debated

claim: Open Quantum Safe provides production-ready implementations.
description: OQS provides prototypes, not production-ready code

claim: The transition to PQC will take approximately 10-20 years.
ML-KEM-768 provides security equivalent to AES-192.
description: Supported fact about ML-KEM security levels
